scope: Theorem 11.1 (Maximal Bochner–Riesz bounds and almost-everywhere summation) of the manuscript “Critical local smoothing for the three-dimensional wave equation” (preprints/Critical-local-smoothing-for-the-three-dimensional-wave-equation-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 079 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 79299093c07ea305), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 160-161. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 3 ≤ p < ∞ and δ > 1 − 3/p. Then ∥Bδ ∗f∥Lp(R3) ≤ Cp,δ∥f∥Lp(R3) (f ∈ S(R3 )). (11.1) The family has a bounded maximal extension to Lp(R3), and in that extension every f ∈ Lp(R3) satisfies lim R→∞ Bδ Rf(x) = f(x) for almost every x ∈ R3 . (11.2) 160 In particular, every δ > 0 is allowed when p = 3.
